title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is section 4° of a long bookkeeping chapter in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The ambient setting, as far as the neighbouring pages show, is a group G_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms attached to a 'rigidified' pair (ρ, σ). Here ρ and σ are finite-order elements generating a modular-type group, presumably a profinite or discrete completion of SL2(Z) or PSL2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3, with U_ρ, U_σ the (pro)cyclic subgroups they generate. G_{ρ,σ} carries several structures: characters ε_2, ε_3, χ with values in μ (presumably {±1}); an 'orientation-preserving' subgroup 𝔊^+; and maps δ_Z to a group γ_{ρ,σ}, with Γ_{ρ,σ} on the next page (probably the arithmetic/Galois-type quotient).

(53) N_ρ is the set of a in G_{ρ,σ} with a(ρ) = ρ^{ε_3(a)}, and N_σ the set of b with b(σ) = σ^{ε_2(b)}. These are the normalizers of U_ρ and U_σ, made explicit through the 'exponent' characters ε_3, ε_2.

The NB announces that a later definition of N_ρ, N_σ will make sense in more general groups, referring back to remarks on pp. 580 and 588 about a 'rigid' (intercommuting?) pair.

(54) Z_ρ is the centralizer of ρ in G_{ρ,σ}, equal to the centralizer of U_ρ and to Ker(ε_3 restricted to N_ρ). Likewise Z_σ = Cent(σ) = Cent(U_σ) = Ker(ε_2 restricted to N_σ).

(55) SZ_ρ = Z_ρ ∩ 𝔊^+ = Ker(δ_Z : Z_ρ → γ_{ρ,σ}) = Cent_{𝔊^+}(ρ) = Cent_{𝔊^+}(U_ρ), and similarly for σ. A marginal note says SN_ρ, SN_σ could be defined the same way but coincide with SZ_ρ, SZ_σ.

(56) There are exact sequences 1 → Z_ρ → N_ρ → μ (→ 1) and 1 → Z_σ → N_σ → μ → 1.

(57) Surjectivity, and in fact a splitting, comes from a distinguished element τ' in N_ρ ∩ N_σ with ε_2(τ') = ε_3(τ') = χ(τ') = -1. This is an orientation-reversing involution inverting both ρ and σ, the analogue of diag(1,-1) in GL2(Z) or of complex conjugation. Hence, as the margin says, N_ρ and N_σ are semidirect products of Z_ρ, Z_σ by μ_{τ'} = {1, τ'}. A reference to p. 580 follows.

The purpose is to set up the lattice of normalizers, centralizers and decomposition-type subgroups of the two elliptic points (orders 2 and 3). This lattice is drawn in diagrams (58)–(59) on the next page, followed by the ♮-versions intersected with 𝔊^♮ and exact sequences onto Γ_{ρ,σ} (61). It is part of Grothendieck's analysis of the Galois/Teichmüller action on the modular tower via the two elliptic points.
errors: The margin claims SN_ρ = SZ_ρ and SN_σ = SZ_σ. Yet on the next page's diagram (59), D_ρ ↪ SN_ρ ∩ SZ_σ and SN_ρ appear as objects distinct from SZ_ρ. Either the marginal remark is a later correction (all elements of 𝔊^+ having ε = 1 on these subgroups) or the two passages are inconsistent; not resolvable from this page.
In (56), the first sequence's '→ 1' at the end appears struck out or illegible, while the second has it. By (57) both should end with → 1 and be split.

If σ has order 2, ε_2(b) is not determined by b(σ) = σ^{ε_2}. So implicitly σ has order 4 (SL2-type, σ^2 = ρ^3 central), or ε_2 is defined independently as a character and (53) is a condition rather than a definition. This is a minor implicit assumption.

ideas.what: Normalizers N_ρ, N_σ of the procyclic subgroups generated by the elliptic elements, described via exponent characters ε_3, ε_2 with kernels the centralizers
ideas.modern_name: normalizers/centralizers of finite-order (elliptic, inertia-type) elements in profinite modular or mapping class groups; 'decomposition groups' of elliptic points
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; in anabelian/GT contexts, analysis of normalizers of inertia subgroups appears in Nakamura and others (1990s)

ideas.what: Splitting of 1 → Z → N → μ → 1 by an orientation-reversing involution τ' inverting both ρ and σ, with ε_2 = ε_3 = χ = -1
ideas.modern_name: complex-conjugation / reflection element in the extended modular group PGL2(Z); semidirect product decomposition

ideas.what: Orientation-preserving parts SZ = Z ∩ 𝔊^+ = Ker(δ_Z → γ_{ρ,σ})
ideas.modern_name: restriction to the 'geometric' or orientation-preserving subgroup

deep.surprise_reason: Routine definitions of normalizers and centralizers of the two elliptic generators, plus their splitting by a reflection τ'. This is bookkeeping in a larger unpublished framework, with no new result or connection on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: The superscripts in the heading are the 'natural' sign ♮ (N_ρ^♮, N_σ^♮, Z_ρ^♮, Z_σ^♮), consistent with the next page, not '$'.
In (53) the second line is 'b(σ) = σ^{ε_2}, où ε_2 = ε_2(b)'.

NB line: the asterisked insertion reads roughly '* on donnera une définition de N_ρ, N_σ qui [a un sens] dans certains des groupes plus généraux (Rem. p 580, 588 pour une paire intercommutante [?] ... i.e. rigid...)'.
Margin by (55): 'on définit de façon analogue SN_ρ, SN_σ, mais identiques SN_ρ = SZ_ρ, SN_σ = SZ_σ'.
Margin by (56): 'suites exactes d'où produits semi-directs par μ_{τ'} — les deux produits semi-directs par μ_{τ'}'.
In (56) the first line ends with a crossed-out word after μ; the labels are ε_3 and ε_2.
